enquiry: We read the supplied LED NIR kidney study and want to use the same concept to guide tumor boundary decisions during live surgery. Can we quote its findings as proof that the proposed sensor is ready for that use? We have no new in vivo data and no validation on our own setup. What assessment and next feasibility steps are appropriate?

clarification_questions.question: What decision during surgery should the real-time signal drive, and what goes wrong today when the boundary is judged without it?
clarification_questions.why: Defines the clinical decision and whether an optical signal can support it.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Decision and current pain unclear; treat as an exploratory research question until the surgical decision is defined.

clarification_questions.question: Which tissue contrast must be detected at the boundary (tumor versus which healthy tissue), and at what level of detail is it needed?
clarification_questions.why: Determines whether the contrast seen in the kidney study is relevant to the new target.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Target contrast undefined; the kidney study result cannot be assumed to transfer until the tissue pair is specified.

clarification_questions.question: Which tissue types and optical conditions (blood, fat, moisture, surface state) are expected at the surgical site?
clarification_questions.why: Tissue optics vary strongly and change NIR signals and calibration.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Optical conditions unknown; the kidney study's sample conditions are not assumed to apply.

clarification_questions.question: How will the probe be used in the operating environment, including contact, sterilization and handling constraints?
clarification_questions.why: Determines probe design, cleaning method and feasibility in the clinic.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Sterilization and contact constraints unknown; no sensor design is assumed.

clarification_questions.question: Where would the analyzer sit relative to the surgical field, and what fiber or probe connection is planned?
clarification_questions.why: Defines fiber type and whether a remote analyzer is needed.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Analyzer location unknown; no fiber type or distance is assumed.

clarification_questions.question: What reference method (for example histopathology) will confirm tumor boundaries, and what is its accuracy?
clarification_questions.why: Without a reference, no accuracy can be established for the sensor.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference method unknown; feasibility cannot be judged until the gold standard is defined.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy, response time and regulatory route (in vitro, ex vivo or clinical study) are required before any surgical use?
clarification_questions.why: Sets the gap between the current evidence and what is needed.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Requirements undefined; the work is treated as research only, with no clinical use planned.

flags_before_revision.detail: not_supported: The claim cites 'selectivity is rated low' for fluorescence, but the table rows for fluorimetry (r18, r19) show low selectivity only for fluorimetry, and the caveat about needing a fluorescent tissue component is supported by S01 p.6/S04 p.4; however the cited set includes many unrelated NIR/Raman/UV-Vis rows that do not address fluorescence, so the page support for the fluorescence-specific selectivity rating is only partially shown. Fix: Cite only the fluorimetry rows (TABLE:r18, TABLE:r19) and S04 p.4 for the fluorescent-component requirement, and state that selectivity is rated low for fluorimetry in the source table.

not_supported: The claim states a fiber-link rule check: NIR Vis-NIR silica covers 0.78-2.4 um and FLUO UV-Vis silica covers the nominal range. S02 p.6 gives Vis-NIR silica 350-2400 nm and UV-VIS silica 190-1200 nm, which supports the numbers, but S01 p.10 and p.12 do not discuss fiber transmission ranges; the claim presents 'covers the nominal range' without checking the nominal fluorescence range, which the cited pages do not establish. Fix: Keep only the fiber transmission values from S02 p.6 and state that the fluorescence coverage depends on the excitation and emission wavelengths of the specific fluorophore, which the cited pages do not give.

not_supported: S03 p.7 states that biopsy size, tissue-type differences and sample position may cause strong spectral variability; it does not say that probe position changes can mimic tissue differences in discrimination, so the mimicking claim goes beyond the page. Fix: Rephrase to say that sample position and biopsy differences may produce strong spectral variability that could be confused with tissue differences, citing S03 p.7 for variability only.

overstated: S03 p.14 says the LED number and wavelengths should be adapted to each case individually; the claim that they 'must be re-selected from full-spectrum data' is a stronger prescription than the page's suggestion, and the full-spectrum re-selection method is described on p.10 rather than p.14. Fix: State that LED set should be adapted to each tissue type as suggested in S03 p.14, and cite S03 p.10 for the full-spectrum simulation approach.

rule_hints: evidence_scope: A published application or a laboratory / in-vitro study is a reason to test a method, not proof that it works for a new customer, a process, or clinical use. [DOCX §3; S03 p.3, p.10, p.14]
nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [DOCX §3; DOCX §5]
same_spot_for_heterogeneous: For heterogeneous or fast-changing samples, methods should measure the same spot at the same time, e.g. with a combi probe. [S01 p.8; S04 p.2]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [DOCX §3]
